description: Repos with maintained release branches also set baseBranchPatterns, e.g. ["$default", "/^rel-/"].
Off by default in Renovate; without this, the hook revs pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml never get update PRs.

poetry.description: We don't use Poetry, and its manager takes PEP 621 pyproject.toml files away from pep621.

packageRules.description: Do not hold back our own Actions, reusable workflows and images: the cooldown is for third-party code, and our refs pinned to a branch (e.g. `@<sha> # main`) have no release timestamp, so the cooldown would block their digest updates forever.
Same for our own PyPI and npm packages, whose names lack the DIRACGrid/ prefix.
Group all GitHub Actions updates together.

Third-party Actions pinned to a branch (e.g. `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@<sha> # release/v1`) have no release timestamp, so with the default `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour` (timestamp-required) their digest updates would be held forever. Let them through; versioned refs (`# v4.2.0`) keep the cooldown.
Group all pre-commit hook updates together, instead of one PR per hook.

Lock file maintenance re-resolves everything to the newest version and skips minimumReleaseAge, so only the package manager can enforce a cooldown. pixi does it with `exclude-newer = "7d"` in pixi.toml / [tool.pixi.workspace] (set it in every pixi repo); npm has no rolling equivalent, so its lock files are not refreshed blindly.

Never bump the CI interpreter version (python-version in GitHub Actions workflows): it is a deliberate choice, e.g. pinned to 3.11 while the pre-commit hooks predate the removal of ast.Str in Python 3.12. The environments tested per python version are defined by pixi, not here.
We use the DIRACGrid/tornado (iostreamConfigurable) and DIRACGrid/tornado_m2crypto forks instead of upstream tornado; never bump tornado from PyPI.
Major pre-commit hook updates change code formatting (e.g. black): keep them visible on the dependency dashboard, but require explicit approval before a PR is opened.
